questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Iran about 1,648,195 square kilometres; Slovakia about 49,034 square kilometres; North Macedonia about 25,713 square kilometres; Lebanon about 10,452 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Tehran?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Iran is Tehran.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Iran?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Iran is the Iranian rial.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Iran?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Iran article.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Iran?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Iran article.

questions.proof: The majority of the population talks Persian (also known as Farsi), yet most of the population also speaks such languages as Azeri, Kurdish, and Luri.
